intro: You're looking for a commercial mortgage and want to find a top broker near you. Whether you're buying business premises, refinancing an investment property or funding a new venture, a broker can help you understand your options. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK mortgage broker who will quote you directly.
need_heading: What people searching for a top commercial mortgage near me usually need
need_lead: Most people want a broker who knows the commercial market and can find the right lender for their situation.
needs: You are buying business premises and need a mortgage that suits your company's trading history and the property.
You want to refinance an existing commercial mortgage to get better terms or release equity.
You are an investor looking to purchase a commercial property and need a broker who understands investment mortgages.
You have been turned down by your bank and need a broker who can approach other lenders.
You want a local broker who can meet you face to face and explain the process clearly.
context: Commercial mortgages are different from residential ones. Lenders look closely at both the business and the property, and deposits are usually larger. Most commercial lending is unregulated, so you have fewer protections than with a residential mortgage.

Mortgage advice is regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA). Any broker or adviser you use should be authorised, or be an appointed representative of an authorised firm, and you can check this on the FCA register. Advisers typically hold a qualification such as CeMAP.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: The type of commercial property you are looking to buy or refinance, such as office, retail, industrial or mixed-use.
Whether you are purchasing, refinancing or releasing equity.
The approximate value of the property and the amount you need to borrow.
How much deposit or equity you have available.
The trading history and financial position of your business, if you are buying through a company.
Your preferred location and whether you want a broker who can meet in person.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the mortgage broker
questions: Are you authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority, and can you provide your firm reference number?
Do you search the whole of the market or a limited panel of lenders?
How are you paid, and will you disclose all fees in writing?
What experience do you have with commercial mortgages for businesses like mine?
What information will you need from me to approach lenders?
How long does the process typically take from application to offer?

faqs.q: How do I judge if a commercial mortgage broker is top?
faqs.a: There is no official ranking, so you should check that the broker is authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority and ask about their experience with commercial mortgages. A good broker will explain their approach clearly and tell you whether they search the whole market or a limited panel.

faqs.q: Can iComply recommend a broker near me?
faqs.a: iComply introduces you to a suitable UK mortgage broker based on your needs. We are not regulated and do not give advice, but we can connect you with a broker who will quote you directly.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a commercial mortgage and a residential one?
faqs.a: Commercial mortgages are for business premises or investment property, and lenders assess both the business and the property. Deposits are usually larger, and most commercial lending is unregulated, so you have fewer protections than with a residential mortgage.

faqs.q: Do I need a deposit for a commercial mortgage?
faqs.a: Yes, lenders typically require a deposit, and it is usually larger than for a residential mortgage. The exact amount depends on the lender and the property, so a broker can explain what to expect for your situation.

extra_heading: Weighing up brokers when you want the top commercial mortgage near you
extra: Searching for a top commercial mortgage near me usually means you want someone local who can sit down with you and talk through the property and the business behind it. Distance matters most if you would rather meet face to face, but a broker further away can still handle a commercial case well by phone and email, so decide early how much local presence you actually want.

Because there is no official ranking of commercial mortgage brokers, judge each one on what they can show you. Check their entry on the FCA register, ask how many commercial cases they handle and of what kind, and ask them to explain in plain terms how they would approach your purchase or refinance. A broker who is clear about their lender panel and their fees is easier to compare than one who simply calls themselves the best.

Remember that most commercial lending is unregulated, so the protections you may be used to from a residential mortgage do not all apply here. That makes the broker's explanation of the terms, the deposit and the lender's view of your business especially important. Take your time, ask for anything you do not understand in writing, and do not feel rushed into a decision.

extra_faqs.q: Does a commercial mortgage broker need to be near me?
extra_faqs.a: Not necessarily. Many brokers work with clients across the UK by phone and email, and what matters more is their experience with commercial lending and the type of property you have in mind. A local broker can be helpful if you want to meet in person, but it is not essential.

extra_faqs.q: How can I compare commercial mortgage brokers fairly?
extra_faqs.a: Check that each broker is authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority, ask whether they search the whole market or a limited panel, and ask how they are paid. Then compare how clearly they explain your options and what information they need from you. There is no official ranking, so your own questions are the best way to judge.

extra_faqs.q: Will a broker near me definitely get me a commercial mortgage?
extra_faqs.a: No broker can promise that. Lenders assess both the business and the property, and deposits are usually larger than for a residential mortgage. A broker can present your case well and approach suitable lenders, but the decision rests with the lender.
